comments.note: partials.ts, conditionals.ts, variables.ts, and postProcessor.ts were pre-created by WP-001 with correct implementations — the task naming in WP-001 scope matched WP-002 deliverables exactly. The WP-001 scaffold used a different naming scheme (per-function files) from the original plan.md (which proposed template-engine.ts, post-processors.ts, serializers.ts as consolidated files). The per-function approach is actually cleaner for tree-shaking and was adopted as-is.

The vitest.config.ts in the ai-persona-builder-STABLE project sets passWithNoTests: true, which is good for the scaffold phase but should be reviewed when the project is near-complete — keeping it active could silently hide missing test files.

The resolveVariables() signature accepts Record<string, unknown> for the context parameter (correct for TypeScript strict mode) but the original JS used plain Object. The console.warn calls in partials.ts and variables.ts are the only observable side effects; consider an injectable logger interface in a future WP to make these functions fully pure/testable without spying on console.

comments.note: resolveVariables() treats null values as resolvable (substitutes 'null' via String(null)) because the guard is `context[varName] !== undefined`, and null !== undefined. Only truly-absent keys or explicit undefined are treated as missing. This is consistent behaviour but differs from how some users might expect null to behave (like undefined). Worth documenting in JSDoc.

resolvePartials() self-reference guard works correctly: a partial whose content contains its own marker ({{> a}} → '{{> a}}') hits depth-2 and stops without infinite recursion. The marker is left as-is at depth limit. Verified via QA edge-case test.

resolveConditionals() handles inline blocks (no surrounding newlines) correctly — the \n* prefix in the regex makes leading newlines optional. Both truthy and falsy paths behave as expected for zero-newline context.

serializeTools() does not escape single quotes inside tool names (e.g. "Tool's" → "['Tool's']" which is invalid YAML). This is an acceptable known limitation since tool names in practice are plain alphanumeric identifiers, but worth noting for future robustness.
No imports whatsoever in any engine module — not even node builtins. All five engine modules are completely self-contained. This is excellent for tree-shaking and portability.
